newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Aug 1.

text.p: This daily press summary is produced for Reuters by the
Broadcast Monitoring Company, which is responsible for its
contents.
-- INSIDER CHOSEN AS BANK DEPUTY

Chancellor Gordon Brown strengthened the position of the governor of the Bank of England, Eddie George, by appointing a bank insider as deputy governor. The appointment of Mervyn King, chief economist at the bank, could help to smooth the sometimes turbulent relationship between the bank and the chancellor.
-- FILM FUNDS THREATENED BY LOTTERY EDUCATION PROPOSALS

Plans to develop the British film industry could be under threat due to government proposals to introduce a sixth lottery 'good cause' devoted to health and education. Internal Arts Council memos suggest there may be sharp reductions to the amount of money available to the council from the National
Lottery over the next four years.
-- NEW COMPETITION AUTHORITY PLANNED

The Monopolies and Mergers Commission is to be replaced by a new body with wider powers, Margaret Beckett announced Friday. The Competition Commission will take on the functions of the MMC and also hear appeals against decisions of the director general of trading under a tough competition regime to be introduced
next year.
-- GOLDMAN CONSORTIUM TO RUN DSS PROPERTY

A consortium led by Goldman Sachs International has been selected to take over the Department of Social Security's 700-building estate under the largest single private finance initiative deal yet concluded. However, ministers have abandoned the previous government's plans to use the PFI to refurbish the Treasury's Whitehall headquarters because they felt the scheme was inappropriate at a time of spending constraint.
-- GOVERNMENT SIGNALS BACKING FOR FUTURE LARGE AIRCRAFT

The government has ended months of speculation within the aerospace industry by signalling that it plans to buy between 40 and 50 military transport aircraft from the European Airbus consortium. George Robertson announced Thursday that he was predisposed to buy the Future Large Aircraft in a two billion stg deal that would secure thousands of jobs in Britain and Europe.
-- SURVIVORS OF ABERFAN TRAGEDY TO BE REPAID 150,000 STG

The government has announced it will repay 150,000 stg to survivors of the Aberfan tragedy, even though the money spent in 1966 would now amount to 1.5m stg. But residents of the town who have campaigned for the repayment are philosophical. "An injustice has been put right at last," said Cliff Minnett, a former miner and chairman of the Aberfan Memorial committee.
-- CHARITIES HIT BY SWITCH TO FIDS

Charities are losing investment income as a result of budget changes that have encouraged a growing number of companies to change the way they pay dividends. Some charities have said they may need to change their investment policy and avoid buying shares in the companies concerned. Many companies are now paying foreign income dividends that do not allow tax exempt investors
like charities to reclaim tax.
-- RAIL UNIONS THREATEN STRIKES OVER GUARD SKILLS

RMT rail union is threatening strikes that could affect services across the nation in a dispute over the future role of guards. The union says it will ballot 6,000 of its members over the next few weeks with a closing date of September 2. Any industrial action, most likely a series of one day strikes, would come a week later. The union fears that any reduction in role for guards would unacceptably compromise the safety of
passengers and rail workers.
-- ZANTAC DECLINE AND STRONG POUND HIT GLAXO

The UK's leading drugs company, Glaxo Wellcome released its half-year results on Thursday, which illustrated the adverse effects of the strong pound and a reduction in sales of its ulcer treatment drug, Zantac. Pre-tax profits at Glaxo were down from 1.55 billion stg to 1.52 billion, turnover fell from 4.2 billion stg to 4.1 billion stg, and earnings per share fell from 29.7p to 29.4p. Excluding currency changes, sales of drugs in the first half launched since 1990 were up 50 percent.
-- LOGICA TO BUY ALDISCON FOR 51M STG

Software group Logica has announced its 51 million stg acquisition of network systems company Aldiscon, to be funded by a rights issue, in a move that will lead to 20 percent of the group being telecommunications related. Logica chief executive Martin Read said the acquisition would "enhance Logica's ability to develop and deploy repeatable software solutions in the telecoms sector", and analysts believe it will lift the group's yearly earnings by a couple of percentage points.
